name: CR-Diff-02-linearity-5.a
questiontext: Use the laws of logarithms to find the following derivative: \[ \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}} \left[\ln({{CT:1}})\right]. \] [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: Using the laws of logarithms alg_logarithms we get \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \ln({{CT:1}}) &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:2}}{{CT:3}} \end{array}\] So, by linearity calc_diff_linearity_rule, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[\ln({{CT:1}})\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:2}}\frac{d}{dx}[{{CT:3}}] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:2}}{{CT:4}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}} \end{array}\]
